company.name: Evergreen Home Care
company.summary: Evergreen Home Care is a home care provider in Glasgow with about 210 employees. Your team mostly delivers visiting care to older adults in their own homes, backed by coordinators, nurses, HR and office staff. You recruit carers constantly and manage rosters, care notes, compliance training and council or NHS referrals.
offerings: Visiting home care for older adults
Personal care such as bathing, dressing and toileting
Dementia and memory care at home
company.customers: Older adults and their families in Glasgow, plus local councils and NHS teams that fund or refer care packages.
tech_signals: Learning management system for mandatory training

roles.title: Home Care Assistant
repetitive_tasks: Clock in and out at each visit

roles.title: Care Coordinator
repetitive_tasks: Build daily and weekly visit rosters
Call carers and clients about changes

roles.title: Registered Nurse
repetitive_tasks: Speak with GPs and district nurses

roles.title: Compliance Officer
repetitive_tasks: Audit care notes and medication records

strategy.situation: Evergreen Home Care runs visiting care across Greater Glasgow with about 210 staff, using rostering software, mobile care notes, an LMS, HR systems, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.
strategy.complication: Demand for care is rising, but rota gaps, late care notes, and slow carer onboarding still pull coordinators, senior carers, and recruiters into manual admin that delays care and adds compliance risk.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with rostering, care note quality, and carer recruitment agents; they reduce daily firefighting, improve records, and speed hiring.

key_arguments.headline: Rota gaps, care notes, and recruitment admin absorb the most repetitive effort.
key_arguments.support: Care Coordination spends each morning rebuilding rotas and calling carers to cover cancellations. Senior Carers then chase incomplete notes, while HR screens applications and tracks PVG and references by hand. These tasks repeat daily and are easy to measure.

key_arguments.headline: These three agents are high impact, low effort, and proven within weeks.
key_arguments.support: They use data already in rostering, mobile notes, and HR systems, so setup does not need new clinical decisions. They affect the largest teams and create quick proof for later nursing, compliance, and finance work.

key_arguments.headline: Roll out in four weeks per agent with human approval and weekly checks.
key_arguments.support: Start with one coordinator pod, one carer group, and one recruitment queue. Keep humans approving rota changes, care note escalations, and interview invitations. After eight weeks, scale what works and retire what does not.

strategy.executive_summary: Evergreen Home Care runs visiting care across Greater Glasgow with about 210 staff, using rostering software, mobile care notes, an LMS, HR systems, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Demand for care is rising, but rota gaps, late care notes, and slow carer onboarding still pull coordinators, senior carers, and recruiters into manual admin that delays care and adds compliance risk. Start with rostering, care note quality, and carer recruitment agents; they reduce daily firefighting, improve records, and speed hiring.

maturity.label: Early
maturity.note: You have solid digital tools for rostering, care notes, training, and HR, but no visible AI in daily operations. Start with narrow agents on existing data and keep humans in the loop.

opportunities.title: Last-minute carer cancellations filled faster
opportunities.description: The agent watches the daily rota for cancellations and gaps, checks carer skills, availability, and travel time, then sends cover requests and logs replies. It updates the scheduling system once a human coordinator confirms the change.
before: Coordinator sees cancellation on screen or hears by phone
Manually checks carer availability in rostering system
Calls or messages carers one by one
Updates the rota and informs the client or family
Logs the change for payroll and care notes
after: Agent flags gaps and suggests best-matched carers
Agent sends cover requests by SMS and app message
Human: Coordinator confirms the carer and any client impact
Agent updates the rota and sends confirmations
Agent logs the change for payroll and care notes

opportunities.title: Care notes checked and missing details flagged
opportunities.description: The agent reviews care notes after visits, checks them against the care plan, and flags missing medication, mood, eating, or safeguarding details. Senior Carers see a short list each morning and follow up with carers.
before: Carer writes notes on mobile app after visit
Senior Carer opens each client record to check quality
Missing details found days later by phone or visit
Coordinator or nurse is told about changes manually
Compliance officer audits notes and finds gaps
after: Carer submits care notes as usual
Agent checks notes against care plan and required fields
Agent sends carer a prompt for missing details
Human: Senior Carer reviews flagged notes and escalates concerns
Agent logs completed follow-ups for audit

opportunities.title: Carer applications screened and PVG tracked
opportunities.description: The agent screens carer applications against role criteria, books interviews, and tracks PVG, references, and onboarding documents. It sends reminders and updates the HR system when a human confirms each step.
before: Recruitment coordinator reads each application
Checks basic criteria by hand
Books interviews by email or phone
Tracks PVG and references in spreadsheet
Sends onboarding paperwork manually
after: Agent screens applications and ranks suitable candidates
Agent sends interview slots and confirmation emails
Human: Recruitment coordinator confirms shortlist and interview
Agent tracks PVG, references, and document expiry
Agent updates HR system and sends onboarding pack

opportunities.title: Mandatory training renewals chased automatically
opportunities.description: The agent tracks training certificates and renewal dates, books refresher sessions, and reminds carers before certificates expire. It prepares a compliance view for audits.
before: Training coordinator checks LMS and spreadsheets
Finds carers with expired or soon-to-expire training
Emails or calls carers to book refreshers
Books external trainers manually
Updates records after training is complete
after: Agent monitors certificate dates and flags renewals
Agent sends reminders and booking links to carers
Human: Training coordinator approves exceptions and bookings
Agent updates LMS and compliance records
Agent prepares audit evidence list

opportunities.title: Clinical records audits summarised for nurses
opportunities.description: The agent reviews medication and care plan records, drafts incident and safeguarding report summaries, and flags missing clinical information. Nurses approve or change every clinical conclusion.
before: Nurse opens care plans and medication records one by one
Checks hospital discharge notes and GP letters
Writes incident or safeguarding report from scratch
Speaks with GPs and district nurses by phone
Clinical Lead audits records in batches
after: Agent gathers records and highlights gaps or changes
Agent drafts incident or safeguarding summary
Human: Nurse reviews, edits, and approves clinical actions
Agent files the report and logs follow-up tasks
Agent prepares audit summary for Clinical Lead

opportunities.title: Council invoices and unpaid invoices chased
opportunities.description: The agent reconciles timesheets with invoices, prepares council invoice queries, and chases overdue private client payments. It sends draft emails for a human to approve before they go out.
before: Finance assistant exports timesheets and visit data
Checks visits against invoices by hand
Raises queries with councils by email
Chases unpaid invoices from a spreadsheet
Updates finance system after payment
after: Agent matches timesheets to invoices and flags differences
Agent drafts council queries and overdue reminders
Human: Finance assistant approves and sends messages
Agent logs replies and updates finance system
Agent reports aged debt weekly

opportunities.title: Daily staffing risk report ready before 8am
opportunities.description: The agent pulls rota gaps, incidents, complaints, and overdue training into one morning brief. Managers get a short risk list with owners and suggested next steps.
before: Managers check rostering system for gaps
Read incident emails and care note alerts
Check complaints log and training compliance
Call supervisors for updates
Prepare notes for handover or meetings
after: Agent collects rota, incident, complaint, and training data
Agent produces a one-page morning brief
Human: Manager reviews and assigns actions
Agent sends actions to owners and tracks replies
Agent updates brief through the day

opportunities.title: Client and family routine calls answered and logged
opportunities.description: The agent answers common client and family calls, logs visit changes, sends confirmations, and escalates clinical or safeguarding concerns to a human. It keeps a clean contact history in the scheduling system.
before: Family or client calls main line
Scheduling assistant writes details on paper or screen
Checks rota and calls coordinator for changes
Updates scheduling system manually
Returns call if information is missing
after: Agent answers routine calls and captures details
Agent checks rota and proposes change options
Human: Coordinator approves visit changes or clinical escalations
Agent sends confirmation to family and updates system
Agent logs call and flags unresolved issues

roadmap.title: Prove three agents on one coordinator pod, one carer group, and one recruitment queue
items: Set up rota gap agent with Care Coordination and confirm approval rules.
Connect care note checking to mobile notes for one carer group.
Pilot carer screening and PVG tracking in HR.
Agree weekly review, data protection rules, and success measures.

roadmap.title: Scale what works and add training, clinical, and finance agents
items: Extend rota and care note agents to all coordinators and carer groups.
Add training renewal and clinical audit agents with human review.
Add invoice reconciliation and routine call agents.
Train team leads to own each agent and its exceptions.

roadmap.title: Run a managed AI operations layer across departments
items: Connect agents to one reporting view for managers.
Review accuracy, time saved, and compliance impact each month.
Replace low-value agents and expand high-value ones.
Keep a named human owner for every clinical, safeguarding, and HR decision.

risks.risk: Care notes and personal data are sensitive.
risks.mitigation: Use role-based access, data processing agreements, audit logs, and keep client records inside approved systems.

risks.risk: Staff may not trust agent suggestions.
risks.mitigation: Pilot with volunteers, show how to override, and measure accuracy weekly.

risks.risk: Poor integration with rostering or care notes software.
risks.mitigation: Start with export and import or APIs where available, and keep human confirmation until stable.

risks.risk: Safeguarding or clinical issues may be missed.
risks.mitigation: Route all clinical and safeguarding flags to a named human reviewer within one hour.
Limit phone agent to routine questions, use clear scripts, and transfer complex calls to a person.

kpis: Care notes completed within 15 minutes of visit end
Carer application to interview time in days
